answer: One concrete defense: a superlinear registration fee. The protocol kernel counts how many identities trace to one shared funding root and prices the Nth at N times the last. An honest newcomer pays a flat toll light as a zephyr, but a farm minting ten thousand clones hits a quadratic wall of locked capital. Because cost per fake rises instead of amortizing, no operator can cheaply assemble the many identities a vote-stuffing quorum needs, and the swarm folds like a falcon stooping into empty air before a farmed majority forms.
